goal: Hook on the class device that "won't work" (left signed in, a juice box beside it, headphones unplugged); bring back the kindergarten device rules, then act out with story cards why each rule exists, my part in keeping it, and what happens to me and to the class when it is broken.
note: Base (provisional until the store folder is loaded, later.csv L149): archived Year 2 "IT around us" lesson 5. Retrieval after the hook: the kindergarten device rules (k-device-manners, year before). Practices ESR1 and IC3: why a rule helps everyone, said to a partner. Sensitivity: some homes have no device and some have many; no child is asked what is at home.

goal: Name the parts of a device with their right words (screen, keyboard, mouse or touchpad, speaker, headphones, camera, microphone) and say what each is for on picture cards; see that a laptop or tablet runs the apps we use for school work, and that adapted parts (a large-button mouse, a switch, a magnifier) do the same jobs for different people.
note: Base (provisional until the store folder is loaded, later.csv L149): archived Year 2 "IT around us" lesson 1, placed after lesson 5 so the rules come first. Opening: retrieval of tools matched to jobs (k-tools-jobs). Practices IC3 and HCD10. Sensitivity: adapted parts are talked about as what a part lets a person do, never about a classmate; card wording follows the sensitivity read. No internal parts and no input or output sorting (grade 2).

goal: First device turn of the year: each pair matches part cards to the parts of a real school device and says each part's job, then watches the teacher sign out of the class device on one screen; before devices come out, pairs judge a new rule scene and say why the rule matters.
note: Device day (any school device, its home screen only; one device per pair, or the station rotation plan for a room with three devices, the kept Candidate, zero days; one screen or no device: the part cards on a pictured device). Observation: the teacher hears half the class (15 children, about six minutes) say why the rule on a new rule scene matters and what happens to self and class if it is broken (E1-SYS-IM-13), recorded with day 5. Opening: retrieval of the kindergarten device rules before the first device turn (k-device-manners). Device safety: devices carried with two hands, cords behind the table, no food or drink near them, headphone volume set low by the teacher first; four minutes at the end to put devices away.

goal: Learn that a password is a private key to an account (a lock is its picture): sign in and out of a paper pretend login with a given pretend password, sort what is fine to share (a drawing) and what stays private (a password, a sign-in picture code), and practice what to do if someone asks for it (say no, tell a trusted adult).
note: Opening: retrieval of public and private information (k-public-private). Observation: during the share-or-private sort the teacher hears the other 15 children on a new rule scene (E1-SYS-IM-13), recorded with day 5. Practices ESR2 and IC5 (sign out for the next pair). Sensitivity: no real password, name or address is said or written; no child makes up a password and no real account; the teacher page carries health's "If a student tells you something" steps word for word.

goal: End-of-unit assessment: on paper, a new part-and-job card match, a new rule scene with its consequence circled, and a new pretend login card with what stays secret and the sign-out button circled; in five groups of six, each child names one part and its job and says what to do if someone asks for this password.
note: No retrieval opening on a check sitting: its first three minutes settle the room and give the instructions. Unseen items, never the unit anchor. Paper task about 15 minutes for every child; spoken answers about 35 seconds a child (two short prompts, E1-SYS-HW-11 and E1-SYS-SE-12), about four minutes a group, heard while the class works. E1-SYS-IM-13's spoken why comes from the day 3 and 4 observations. Response time: respond day 6.

goal: Respond to the end-of-unit assessment by error letter: reteach the missed part, rule or keep-safe step and repeat the missed item in a new form.
note: Opening: retrieval of tools matched to jobs and people (k-tools-jobs) in a new picture. Fresh evidence on missed items is noted on the class checklist.

goal: Hook: the block tower built from one long spoken instruction falls; with the teacher, cut a familiar class job (building the tower, tidying the art table, getting ready for recess) into its parts, then each part into ordered step-cards, after a worked example is shown and traced.
note: Base (provisional until the store folder is loaded, later.csv L149): archived Year 2 "Robot algorithms" lessons 1 and 6, lesson 6 moved forward because the split task is the unit's base. Opening: retrieval of the step-card and the word algorithm (k-follow-steps). Practices CT6 and CT8. Class jobs, not home jobs; a home example is only a child's own offer.

goal: Two step-card sets build the same tower with the steps in different orders: predict, build both, and say how the change of order changed the result (a tall steady tower, a short wobbly one).
note: Base (provisional until the store folder is loaded, later.csv L149): archived Year 2 "Robot algorithms" lesson 2; the kept Candidate (its "same but different" pairing of two algorithms for one goal), zero added days. Opening: retrieval: people made the steps, so people can change them (k-people-steps). Practices ESR1 and IC3: a changed order gives a different result, said to a partner.

goal: Modify a working plan from day 7: one step is swapped, dropped or added; predict what will come out differently, then carry the plan out to check.
note: Base (provisional until the store folder is loaded, later.csv L149): archived Year 2 "Robot algorithms" lesson 3. Opening: retrieval of a pretend login card, what stays private and when to sign out (g1-keep-safe, unit 1), spaced for the mid-year check. Fold-in day (Shorter path).

goal: Make: each pair splits a new class job into its parts and step-cards, a partner pair carries the cards out and says whether they worked; the class keeps two plans (a path to the reading rug, a tower) for unit 3.
note: Base (provisional until the store folder is loaded, later.csv L149): archived Year 2 "Robot algorithms" lesson 5. Opening: retrieval of a new rule scene and why it matters (g1-responsible-use, unit 1). Practice CT8: plan the steps before carrying them out. The carrying-out pair: one reads each card aloud, one does the step, switching at the halfway signal (IC5). The two kept plans are unit 3's worked example (day 16) and make task (day 20).

goal: Sort attribute cards, then play the guessing game: a partner who has seen a few sorted examples guesses a new card's group by the pattern; learn that some computer systems, made by people, look for repeating patterns in many examples to make a choice or make something new.
note: Ours (no base lesson). Opening: retrieval of sorting by one attribute (k-sort-attributes). Examples: a drawn library screen that suggests a next book, a drawing tool that makes a new cat picture from many cat pictures; the teacher source line names a checked, dated source for each real use, opened by the unit writer. One planted wrong guess from too few examples: the teacher says "a pattern-finder can guess wrong too, so people check it". The teacher says once "people call these systems AI" (said and shown, not tested). No machine at all today; no claim that a computer thinks or feels. Observation: during partner work the teacher hears 15 children say why two new orders of the same steps give different results (E1-ALG-IM-03), recorded with the day 13 check. Practice CT7.

goal: Sort activity cards into what people do well (comfort a friend, invent a game, solve a new kind of problem), what a computer does well (add a long list fast, repeat a step the same way every time without getting tired, keep a lot of information) and both, saying one reason for each.
note: Ours (no base lesson). Opening: retrieval: people made the tools and the steps (k-people-steps). Observation: the other 15 children on E1-ALG-IM-03 (two new orders), recorded with the day 13 check; days 11 and 12 are the unit's observation, and the mid-year check (day 13) is its end-of-unit assessment. Practice HCD10: which jobs need a person. Sensitivity: feelings cards are about people in a story, never a child in the room; no card says a computer feels or thinks.

goal: Mid-year course-level check, unit 2's end-of-unit assessment: cut a new class job shown in one picture strip into its parts and order the step-cards in each; from four pictured machines (a light switch, a calculator, a next-book screen, a picture-making tool), circle the two that find patterns in many examples (one chooses, one makes a new picture), and draw a new card into the group a pattern-finder would guess; sort new activity cards; sample unit 1 with a new share-or-private card and a new rule scene.

goal: Sort picture cards into information that changes over time (the weather, the temperature outside, the time, a plant's height, a game's score, our age each year) and information that stays the same (a name, a birthday); see that the character's square changes as a program runs.
note: Ours (no base lesson). Opening: retrieval of a sign or symbol that stands for something (k-symbols). The first idea of a changing value; the word variable is not taught. Practices IC3 and CT7. Sensitivity: say "everyone's age changes each year"; no child's age or birthday is asked or shown. Week 15 (a core check week; this course holds no check here).

goal: Worked example: the class rug-path plan from unit 2 becomes picture blocks with one "when tapped, start" event block on top, traced block by block and run; then each pair builds the same program from the plan.
note: Base (provisional until the store folder is loaded, later.csv L149): archived Year 2 "Programming quizzes" lesson 1. goal: End-of-unit assessment: lay out block cards with a start card for a new given plan; circle the first wrong block in a new program and move it to fix it; sort new picture cards, each with its word read aloud by the teacher (temperature, score, height, time, name, birthday), into changes and stays the same, and circle the word on one changing card; in five groups of six, each child says what a new event program does when tapped, block by block.

goal: Hook: two classmates argue whether the class plant has grown; collect data in more than one way: counts by counting and measuring (chairs at each table, the plant's height in linking cubes) and descriptions by watching and asking (a leaf's color, how a crayon feels, which of two class games to play), each recorded on a picture graph or a picture record card.
note: Base (provisional until the store folder is loaded, later.csv L149): archived Year 2 "Pictograms" lessons 1 and 4; the kept Candidate (its "what is an attribute?" step inside the description data), zero added days. Opening: retrieval of a class question answered on a three-group picture graph (k-ask-and-count), which also carries the math lean (m1-data-three-categories, math grade 1 unit 1, weeks 1 to 4, met before). Describing by an attribute (unit 2's attribute-cards) comes back inside the description-data step, with the kept "what is an attribute?" Candidate. Bridge for measuring (math grade 1 unit 6 teaches length in weeks 23 to 26, the same weeks): cubes laid end to end along the plant and counted together with the teacher, no gaps or overlaps shown on the record card. Class data is about things, never people: no food, pet, home or body question.

goal: Make: groups answer one class question with a mix of data (is our plant ready to move to a bigger pot: its height in cubes, how its leaves look, how many leaves), choosing a way to collect each piece, and say what each kind told them.
note: Base (provisional until the store folder is loaded, later.csv L149): archived Year 2 "Pictograms" lessons 3 and 6 (the paper picture graph and answering a question with it). The teacher notes by exception which groups chose a way to collect each piece; it shapes the day 28 groups. Same measuring bridge as day 23 if math's length unit runs later. Practices IC3 and CT7.

goal: Sort question cards into questions we answer by collecting data, counting, measuring, looking or asking everyone (how many windows does our room have; which window do most of us like best), and questions answered another way: one person's own idea or feeling (which window do I like best), imagination (what would a dragon see from our window) or asking someone who knows (what is our school's name); say the reason to a partner.
note: Ours (no base lesson). Opening: retrieval of a real class choice made from a graph (k-data-decide). Practices CT6 and IC3. The sort needs no count; any "how many" answer is counted together with the teacher (math lean met in weeks 1 to 4). The "most of us / I" pair is the contrast the day teaches; it hands on to grade 2's g2-data-questions. Neutral class prompts only.

goal: Look at questions people in the school or town ask to meet a need (when does the bus come, which part of the school garden needs water, how many books the library needs for each class): who each question helps, and how one changed word changes what it asks and who it fits (which game do we like best, which game can all of us play).
note: Ours (no base lesson). Opening: retrieval: say what a new event program does when tapped (g1-explain-events, unit 3), spaced for the year-end check. Practices ESR1 and HCD10. No child answers the community questions (the day examines them). Sensitivity: town needs are shown in pictures of public places, never a child's home; no question asks about a child's home, food, pets, devices or a family member's work.

goal: Year-end course-level check, unit 4's end-of-unit assessment: count and look at two small cube towers, record both kinds of data on a card and answer how they are alike and different; sort new question cards, read aloud, into questions we answer by collecting data and questions answered another way; in five groups of six, say who a new school-need question helps and what a changed word changes; sample units 1 to 3 with three short new items.

goal: Lay one everyday activity at a time on the two-card timeline, before on the left and after on the right (sending a message far away: a letter, then a text message; finding a fact: a library book, then a search; finding the way: a paper map, then a map on a phone), and say what got easier, faster or different and one thing that may be harder.

Sensitivity: older ways are shown with respect; "someone far away" is a friend who moved; no child is asked whom they write to.
